title: Which numbers are factors of 840, using its primes?
description: The primes of eight hundred and forty are reordered into two groups to show that twenty eight is a factor with partner thirty. Fourteen and eight are tested the same way by taking primes from the list. Keeko's doubt, that twenty seven is a factor, is tested by counting threes.
teaching_notes: One idea: a group of the primes of a number, multiplied together, is a factor of it, and a number needing a prime more times than it appears is not. Watch for students who check only that the prime appears, not how many times.

video_script.why: The child can factorise into primes but has not yet used the primes to test whether a number divides another.
video_script.substitution: A number is a factor when each of its primes can be taken from the big number's primes, as many times as it needs.
video_script.anchor: The number eight hundred and forty written as its six primes, two, two, two, three, five and seven.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says twenty seven is a factor because eight hundred and forty has a three. But twenty seven needs three 3s and 840 has only one.
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty eight, fourteen and eight are factors of eight hundred and forty.

final_answer.spoken: twenty eight, fourteen and eight are factors, and twenty seven is not

maths_rules: Regroup: 840 = (2 x 2 x 7) x (2 x 3 x 5) = 28 x 30. So 28 is a factor with partner 30.
14 = 2 x 7 uses one 2 and one 7, both available, so 14 is a factor.
8 = 2 x 2 x 2 uses three 2s, and 840 has three 2s, so 8 is a factor.
27 = 3 x 3 x 3 needs three 3s, but 840 has one 3, so 27 is not a factor.
video_script.design: One idea: a group of the primes of a number is a factor, and the rest of the primes give the partner. Assumes prime factorisation. Wrong idea: twenty seven is a factor because a three is present. The primes stay on the board all video.
